_info: Dataset registry for the fence detector. Every dataset is synthetic and auto-labelled from Gazebo ground truth by tools/make_dataset.py (no hand labels). Images are not in git: they live on the training machine under ~/querra-data/<id> and can be regenerated with the command at the given code commit. Farm seed = --seed + layout number (default --seed 100), so layout 40 is always seed 140. Ids are the folder names. 'role' says how a split may be used: train, val (model selection) or test (never used for training or model selection).

datasets.style: v1
datasets.notes: Random farms: fence shape, post spacing, wire heights, 2-3 broken wires, 1-2 fallen posts, 1-2 branches, herd, sun, grass colour. Camera 5-20 m, tilt 35-80 deg. The dead strand after a break is always grey.

datasets.style: v2
datasets.command: tools/make_dataset.sh --style v2 (layouts 20-29, 300 frames; tests: layouts 40-42, 250 frames; --mission-world layout 90, 400 frames)
datasets.notes: Targets the false broken wire: 3-4 breaks per farm, so long dead strands, drawn in random colours (grey, live yellow, dull, dark) and labelled wire. Three break shapes. 60% of the poses imitate the inspection flight.

datasets.style: v3 (test: v2)
datasets.command: tools/make_dataset.sh --seed 100 --look rich --style v3 --start 200 --layouts 212 --split train --frames 300 (val: --start 212 --layouts 214; test: --style v2 --start 40 --layouts 43 --frames 250; mission: --mission-world --start 90 --layouts 91 --frames 400)
datasets.notes: The rich world (textured grass, terrain, sky): random sun height and strength, sky fill, ambient light, grass tint, one terrain mesh per farm. The test farms use the same seeds as fence_yolo_v2's test, so the two looks are compared on the same farms and pose distribution (not frame-identical: empty frames are skipped).

datasets.style: ground robot side camera
datasets.notes: Test frames were written as G00-G02 at 54f574b (the same names as training layouts 0-2, in another folder) and renamed T00-T02; the generator names test layouts T since the next commit. Random forest enclosures in the style of forest.json (6-9 sided fence, 3.5-5.5 m post spacing, 3-5 broken wires, 2-3 fallen posts, 2-3 branches on the wires, forest density and sun randomised). The camera is a free copy of the ground robot's side camera (640x400, 100 deg hfov) at robot poses: 1.4-2.5 m outside the fence, 0.70 m up, looking left and 6 deg down, with heading, pitch and roll noise. 45% of the poses are near a fault (each fault type equally often). Labels from the known geometry with the drone's 7 classes; a depth camera on the same mount removes hidden parts; nothing farther than 12 m. About a third of the frames without a fault are dropped. No animals in the forest.

datasets.style: ground robot patrol route
datasets.notes: The real forest.json world along the robot's patrol route, one frame every 0.5 m at the nominal camera pose (no noise), with patrol_poses.jsonl and patrol_faults.json (F1-F5). Never used for training or model selection: tools/ground_patrol_eval.py scores faults found and false alerts on it (5 of 8 frames confirm an alert).

datasets.style: ground robot side camera, fallen-post focus
datasets.notes: Extra fallen posts for ground-v0.2: random forest enclosures as in ground_yolo, but with 4-6 fallen posts each (ground_yolo: 2-3), and 70% of the poses near a fault, 70% of those near a fallen post (ground_yolo: 45% near a fault, each type equally often). Labels: post 1290, wire 2465, wire_break 158, fallen_post 536, branch 105. Some layouts have no branch fault: the fallen posts take the places a branch could go. Seeds 520-525 are outside the training (500-513), patrol (700-702) and test (900-902) ranges.

datasets.style: ground robot side camera, fence look classic, 3x supersampled, stream JPEG -q:v 4
datasets.notes: The test forests of ground_yolo (seeds 900-902) with the strands drawn as the classic look (3.6 cm glowing yellow rods), as every model so far was trained on (sim/gen_world.py FENCE_LOOKS). The colour camera rendered at 3x and averaged in linear light, so a wire thinner than a pixel shows as a faint line. Same forests and pose distribution as ground_yolo_stream's test split, but not frame for frame: the strands change what the depth camera hides, and so which frames are kept. Scoring only: ml/runs/ground-v0.2/fence_looks.

datasets.style: ground robot side camera, real fence conductors (steel wire, polywire, polyrope, polytape), 3x supersampled
datasets.notes: Thin wire for ground-v0.3: random forest enclosures as in ground_yolo, with the strands drawn as real conductors at their real size (sim/gen_world.py FENCE_LOOKS), one look per enclosure in the order given to --fence-look: train 6 steel wire (2.5 mm grey), 6 polywire (3 mm yellow), 2 polyrope (6 mm white), 2 polytape (40 mm white); val 1 steel wire, 1 polywire. The colour camera rendered at 3x and averaged in linear light, so a wire thinner than a pixel shows as a faint line. Labels, train: post 4631, wire 6997, wire_break 825, fallen_post 440, branch 783; val: post 613, wire 932, wire_break 140, fallen_post 41, branch 100. Seeds 530-547 are outside the training (500-525), patrol (700-702) and test (900-902) ranges. 54 minutes to render on the Mac.
